title: Prompt for + pin related SUP tickets and customer-impact summary in incident bridge channels
author: Benji Okafor
body: Context: Support/SRE asked for a consistent way to keep customer escalations discoverable after a bridge ends. Today, bridge channels frequently miss links to the SUP ticket(s), and the customer-impact summary gets repeated across Slack/Jira/email with drift. This PR updates incident-bot to (1) prompt the bridge creator for related SUP tickets and a customer-impact summary, (2) post and pin a single "Escalation context" message in the bridge channel, and (3) keep the channel topic synced with SUP links (without including customer names). Behavior: - When a bridge channel is created via the bot (or when the bot detects it has been invited to a newly created bridge channel), the bot posts a message with two required actions: "Add related Jira tickets" (accepts SUP-* and optionally INT-*), and "Add customer impact" (free text w/ guidance). - Once submitted, the bot edits the message into a structured summary and pins it. - The bot also sets the channel topic to include: "SUP: SUP-xxxx, SUP-yyyy" plus a short impact tag (e.g., "impact: elevated 5xx, eu-west") and a link to the escalation playbook section on bridges. - The message includes a reminder not to paste customer-sensitive details; it focuses on symptoms/impact/request IDs. - The message provides a one-click "Update context" action to edit tickets/impact later; updates preserve history in a small "edited" footer line with timestamp + editor. Guardrails: - Only allows keys matching ^SUP-\d+$ (and ^INT-\d+$) unless the user explicitly selects "Add other Jira key" (disabled by default). - If no SUP tickets are provided within 10 minutes, the bot posts a follow-up nudge tagging the bridge creator and the current on-call group (configurable per workspace env). - If channel is moved/renamed into #incidents conventions, the pinned message remains and is re-pinned if it was unpinned. Notes: This is intentionally not doing Jira API lookups (permissions vary and we want to avoid leaking summaries into Jira unintentionally); it’s just linking + standardizing context in Slack. Follow-ups: INT-333 will enforce required fields on the Jira side; this PR is the Slack-side piece. Testing: added unit tests for parsing keys, pin idempotency, and topic formatting; added an integration test stub for Slack modal submissions (mocked Slack client).
commits: incident-bot: add bridge "escalation context" prompt on channel creation
incident-bot: validate SUP/INT keys + normalize input
incident-bot: sync channel topic with SUP links (no customer names)
tests: add coverage for key parsing, topic formatting, pin idempotency
docs: update runbook snippet for bridge creators

review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (request changes, 2026-02-11): "Pinning is great. Two asks: (1) topic should not include account/company names; keep it to SUP keys + generic impact tag; (2) make the pin operation idempotent so retries don’t create multiple pinned messages." Benji Okafor (2026-02-11): "Ack. Updated to remove any free-form customer field from topic and added pin lookup by message metadata so we edit existing instead of posting new." Dylan Brooks (comment, 2026-02-11): "Can we accept INT-* as well? Support often links the internal automation follow-up." Benji Okafor (2026-02-11): "Added optional INT-* support and explicit validation; other keys require a config flag." Owen Phillips (comment, 2026-02-12): "Love the nudge after 10 min. Please make sure it only tags creator + on-call when channel name matches bridge convention." Benji Okafor (2026-02-12): "Done—only triggers for channels created via bot or matching /^bridge-/." Sean Gallagher (approval, 2026-02-12): "Looks aligned with playbook refresh. +1 to merging; will help with post-incident audit trails."
release_notes: Incident bridges now include a pinned "Escalation context" message capturing related SUP tickets and a customer-impact summary; channel topics are auto-updated with SUP links for easier cross-referencing.
